craft_claim: Urgent and fear-based appeals motivate protective action only when the reader perceives an effective, feasible response; without it, urgency produces defensive avoidance or denial.

supporting_evidence.location: Communication Monographs 59(4), pp. 329-349 (threat appraisal versus efficacy appraisal)
supporting_evidence.note: The extended parallel process model separates threat appraisal from efficacy appraisal: when threat is high but perceived efficacy is low, people enter fear-control (avoidance, denial, reactance) rather than danger-control (protective action). Urgency therefore requires a plausible action path.

scope: Health, safety, civic and marketing messages that raise alarm to change behavior.
exceptions: When the message's only goal is attention rather than action, the efficacy gate is weaker, but the ethical burden then rises.
Culturally specific authority and trust can substitute for some explicit efficacy cues, but this is context-dependent.
